title: Kinetics and Chemical Equilibria
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Chemistry: Kinetics and Equilibria Worksheets
standard_text: Collision theory, the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution and catalysts, dynamic equilibrium and Le Chatelier's principle, the equilibrium constant Kc and its calculation from equilibrium amounts.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level chemistry worksheets on kinetics and equilibria: Maxwell–Boltzmann distributions, catalysts, Le Chatelier's principle, Kc expressions and Kc calculations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Kc = products over reactants, with powers.
key_sub: Only temperature changes the value of Kc.
body_html:
How to think about it

Reactions need collisions with at least the activation energy. A catalyst gives a route with a lower Ea; a higher temperature moves the Maxwell–Boltzmann peak right, so many more molecules exceed Ea.

At dynamic equilibrium the forward and backward rates are equal. Le Chatelier: the position shifts to oppose a change. For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, Kc = [C]c[D]d / [A]a[B]b.

Example

Kc for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃?

products over reactants with powers

Answer: [NH₃]² / [N₂][H₂]³

Example

Effect of raising the temperature on an exothermic equilibrium?

the endothermic (backward) direction is favoured

Answer: shifts left, Kc falls

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a catalyst shifts the equilibrium.
  • Forgetting to raise concentrations to their coefficients.
  • Thinking pressure changes Kc.

faq.a: A graph of the number of molecules against their energy. The area under it is the total number of molecules.

faq.q: Does a catalyst change the equilibrium position?
faq.a: No. It speeds up the forward and backward reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached sooner.

items.q: What is the mode of a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution?
c: the most probable energy, at the peak
items.e: The mean energy is a little to the right of the peak.

items.q: What happens to the rate of a gas reaction if the pressure is doubled?
c: it increases, because the particles are closer together
items.e: Higher pressure means higher concentration of gas.

items.q: A catalyst is added to CH<sub>4</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO + 3H<sub>2</sub> (steam reforming) at equilibrium. What happens?

the equilibrium shifts to the left
the position of equilibrium does not change; equilibrium is reached faster
items.e: A catalyst speeds up the forward and backward reactions equally.

items.q: Which part of the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve shows the molecules that can react?
c: the point where the curve starts
the area to the right of the activation energy
the area to the left of the activation energy
items.e: Only these molecules have enough energy.

items.q: A reaction mixture is at equilibrium. More reactant is added. What happens?

the equilibrium shifts to the left
items.e: The system uses up some of the added reactant.

items.q: Increasing the concentration of a reactant…
c: increases the rate because collisions are more frequent
items.e: More particles in the same volume.

items.q: What is Le Chatelier's principle?

items.q: Why is a high pressure expensive in industry?

items.e: Pressures are a compromise between yield and cost.

items.e: A low temperature favours the exothermic forward reaction but is too slow.
